title: System map source
description: The hand-written source of a product's system map (model.json). render_map.py checks a source against this file and renders the front page, the cards and the gaps list from it. Only points, bets, definitions and paths are written here; counts, each path's point, Touches and open work are derived at each render. A key that begins with x_ is the project's own and is ignored.

product.description: The product: the top of the tree.

frame.description: A short paragraph on how the product runs, shown above the diagram.

diagram.description: One simple architecture diagram as lines of plain text, drawn in a code block: the main parts and what flows between them.

bets.description: The product's bets, three to seven.

framework.description: The decision tree above the subjects.

angles.description: For software: Business logic, Interface, Infrastructure, QA. Otherwise three or four that split the product the same way, with QA kept; the renderer flags a map with no angle named QA.

bets.description: Bets that hold for everything under this angle. May be empty.

areas.description: The angle's key areas: where a change is decided. Two to five is usual; the renderer flags fewer than two.

subjects.description: Ids of the subjects decided here; may be empty until a later release. Every subject is in exactly one key area.

app.description: The Business logic subjects. The renderer flags an angle that holds both these and dimensions.

core.description: What the product cannot run without: its base records and the logic built on them.

modules.description: Parts that can be left out while the rest still works, such as a system of record of their own.

dimensions.description: Parts of how the product is engineered: the Interface, Infrastructure and QA subjects. A quality (fast, secure) is not a subject.

loops.description: A loop is a flow that repeats and runs through several subjects, such as sign-up to first use, a sync or a release. May be empty.

nodes.description: Ids of the subjects it runs through, in order.

items.description: One trap. It shows on the card of the subject that owns a cited file, or on every subject of the loop when no subject owns one.

when.description: The situation in which it goes wrong.

then.description: What goes wrong, and what to do about it when that is known.

releases.description: Ordered, the first current. A release is a goal a user can reach end to end, with the items that reach it. With no tracker or roadmap to read, leave the list empty and ask the owner.

by.description: Who set it and when. Leave out when unknown and ask the owner.

id.description: The item's id as the tracker writes it, such as R1.2. No two items share one, in this release or another.

paths.description: The paths it changes or will create. It shows as open work on the card of each subject that owns one.

status.description: next: not started, a decision still to make included. in progress: started, or built and not yet switched on. done: built and in the code, even when the release has not shipped.

items.description: In build order: the first item not done is the next build step.

questions.description: Questions only the owner can answer. The gaps list shows at most seven, those that block the product's point, a release goal or a subject first.

blocks.description: What it blocks: product, a release id, or a subject id. Leave out when it blocks none of these.

id.description: An id: lower-case letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon or hyphen, starting with a letter or digit. No two angles, key areas, subjects, bets, loops, releases, items or questions share one.

path.description: A path inside the repository, relative to its root: no leading slash, no spaces, and no `.` or `..` part.

bet.description: A choice that could have gone another way. One with no reason or no alternative stays and is counted as a gap.

why.description: The recorded reason. A research or document pointer goes here as file:<id> or file:<repository path>.

origin.description: owner: their words and hedges. inferred: what the code or a document implies, in your words, or a quoted statement whose author is unknown. proposed: your own choice, with nothing in the sources behind it.

subject.description: A subject: something a person would change that has its own reason to exist.

point.description: One sentence: why this subject exists. A dimension's point answers its one question.

bets.description: This subject's own choices. May be empty.

parts.description: The things inside the subject a reader would name, each with its point.

guarantees.description: What must stay true. On the QA subject that holds the user journeys, if the product has one: one per journey goal with its acceptance, in lifecycle order.

items.description: One thing that must stay true.

test.description: The test file that proves it. Leave out until the file exists.

home.description: The paths this subject owns, relative to the repository root, each a file or a folder with no trailing slash. Its own tests and documents go here when they are separate files; a test suite or a document shared by many subjects belongs to the QA or Interface subject that keeps it. When paths nest, the longest matching path owns the file. A path that does not exist yet must be named by an item of the current release.

tools.description: Commands or callable operations defined in this subject's own code. The renderer does not find these; list them.

name.description: The command as typed, or the operation's name.

register_ids.description: Its rows in the dimension register, where one exists.

owner.description: Its one owner, copied from the dimension register, where one exists.
